alt: Closed questions give quantitative data and open questions give qualitative data. Three wording traps: leading questions suggest an answer, loaded questions use emotive words, and double-barrelled questions ask two things at once. Below, delivery choices affect response rates.
caption: Every question type and every word choice affects the data a questionnaire produces.

alt: A line from quantitative to qualitative. Structured interviews ask the same questions in the same order, as in Young and Willmott’s survey. Semi-structured interviews add freedom to probe. Unstructured interviews are guided conversations, as Carlen used. Focus groups discuss a topic together. Below, strengths and weaknesses.
caption: The less structured the interview, the more depth and the less comparability.

alt: A two-by-two grid. Overt participant: joining a staff room with permission. Overt non-participant: sitting at the back of a classroom. Covert participant: taking a job without revealing the research. Covert non-participant: watching a public place unnoticed. Overt observation risks the observer effect; covert observation raises consent and deception. Below, going native and ethnography.
caption: Joining or watching, openly or in secret: each choice trades validity against other problems.

after: ## Matching a method to a topic
alt: Five research questions matched to methods: a closed-question questionnaire for how many couples share housework; participant observation for why pupils join anti-school groups; unstructured interviews for domestic violence; a focus group for parents’ views on school choice; and structured interviews for attitudes to crime across age groups.
caption: Choose the method that fits what the question asks: how many, why, or how people experience it.

alt: Two sequences: interviews can help design a questionnaire, or a questionnaire can show the scale of a pattern and identify people to interview. Below, uses such as triangulation and Willis’s combined methods, and limits such as cost and conflicting results.
caption: Numbers show how big a pattern is; words explain why it happens.
